input.question: why people think machines replacing humans is bad if that means we as a society get the same goods without working?
input.ground_truth: The problem is that *because of how we currently run our society* only people with jobs can earn money. Of course in a different economic system we could just share the bounty that the machines make. Unfortunately two such systems that have been tried -- communism and socialism -- have been shown to have a lot of problems, and so are hated by a lot of people. If these topics interest you, check out /r/automate and /r/BasicIncome

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: why people think machines replacing humans is bad if that means we as a society get the same goods without working?

response.prediction:
Okay! Imagine you have a big box of crayons, and you and your friends love to color together every day. Right now, you all take turns coloring and sharing the crayons, and you all feel happy because you made something beautiful as a team.

Now, imagine a robot comes and says, “I can color all the pictures by myself, really fast!” So the robot does all the coloring, and now you and your friends don’t have to color anymore. At first, it seems fun—you still get pretty pictures to look at!

But here’s the thing: when you colored, you felt proud and happy. You learned new things and had fun with your friends. If the robot does all the coloring, you might start to feel bored or sad because you don’t get to use your crayons or be creative anymore. Also, who will make new crayons or fix them when they break? Who will teach others how to color?

So, even though you still get the pretty pictures, you might miss the things that made you happy and help you grow. That’s why some people are worried when machines do everything—because people like to do things, learn, and feel useful too!
